sources.citation: Mühlhäusler, Peter. 1985. External history of Tok Pisin. In Wurm & Mühlhäusler (eds), Handbook of Tok Pisin, 35-64. PL C-70. (hdl 1885/253255)
sources.note: Nothing (social/labour-trade history of the Samoan plantations; a full-text search for stress/accent = one rhetorical use).

sources.citation: Mühlhäusler, Peter. 1985. Internal development of Tok Pisin. In S.A. Wurm & P. Mühlhäusler (eds), Handbook of Tok Pisin (New Guinea Pidgin), 75-166. Pacific Linguistics C-70. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/253268)
sources.note: Uses SPP as the stabilisation-stage predecessor of Tok Pisin but makes no stress statement about SPP; sec. 2.4.4.2.1 'Pronunciation and phonology' (pp. 91-92) is about segmental variation in early Tok Pisin; the stress remarks (p. 88 loss of syllables preceding main stress in Pacific Jargon English; c. p. 122 'in earlier varieties of Tok Pisin the difference of emphasis on stressed and unstressed syllables was very small (cf. Wurm 1977d:513)') concern Jargon English/Tok Pisin, not SPP.

sources.citation: Mühlhäusler, Peter. 1978. Samoan Plantation Pidgin English and the origin of New Guinea Pidgin. In Papers in Pidgin and Creole Linguistics No. 1, 67-119. Pacific Linguistics A-54. Canberra: Australian National University. (hdl 1885/254406)
sources.note: Nothing. The linguistic part (sec. 6, pp. 87-110) covers lexicon, word formation and a syntactic sketch only; note 16 (p. 113): 'No phonological analysis of SPP has been undertaken by the author; the orthography used is that of NGP with some minor changes..'. Only prosodic remark, p. 108 (6.3.8): 'Statements, questions and commands are distinguished by means of intonation.'
